name: Direct West Face
approach: Park at the SR-20 pullout near milepost 166 (about 0.7 mile past the Cutthroat Lake Road turnoff heading west from Winthrop, roughly 3.75 miles east of the Washington Pass hairpin). A climbers' boot path drops steeply off the highway shoulder through loose talus and duff and reaches Early Winters Creek at about 4,080 ft, where log crossings get you across (use caution in early-season high water). From the creek the trail firms up for roughly a quarter mile through forest before angling steeply uphill between two feeder gullies, gaining close to 2,400 ft to a flat bench at about 6,460-6,500 ft below the spires — the standard bivy/staging camp for the Wine Spires. Water here is unreliable late season; some parties find a small seasonal trickle (locally nicknamed 'Jesus Spring') in a dry sandy side-gully near the bench, but don't count on it. From the bench camp, continue up and right (east), passing a couple of minor buttresses, to gain a broad talus/scree gully that runs directly to the base of Pernod's west face — the tallest wall in the Wine Spires. The last few hundred feet of this gully are loose, ball-bearing scree over slab (cairns mark the better line); trekking poles help a lot, and helmets should go on well before entering the gully because of rockfall potential from any party above. All told it's roughly 3,000-3,500 ft of gain over about 2-2.5 miles one-way from the car to the base of the route.

approach_variants.name: The Wine Spires pullout and the bench camp, then up and right past two minor buttresses into the talus gully under the tallest wall
approach_variants.notes:
Park at the SR-20 pullout near milepost 166, about 0.7 mile past the Cutthroat Lake Road turnoff heading west from Winthrop and roughly 3.75 miles east of the Washington Pass hairpin. A climbers' boot path drops steeply off the highway shoulder through loose talus and duff and reaches Early Winters Creek at about 4,080 ft, where log crossings get you across; use caution in early-season high water.

From the creek the trail firms up for roughly a quarter mile through forest before angling steeply uphill between two feeder gullies, gaining close to 2,400 ft to a flat bench at about 6,460-6,500 ft, the standard bivy and staging camp for the Wine Spires. Water there is unreliable late season; some parties find a small seasonal trickle in a dry sandy side-gully near the bench, but do not count on it.

Roughly 3,000-3,500 ft of gain over about 2-2.5 miles one-way from the car to the base.
hazards: The only fixed rappel anchor on the route is on the summit ridge, where nuts have been left in place
Old aid bolts on the route, one reported missing a hanger and another loose in its hole
Ball-bearing scree over slab in the last few hundred feet of the approach gully
A descent onto the opposite side of the spire followed by a substantial re-ascent to Burgundy Col
Unreliable water at the bench camp late season
approach_variants.baseFinding:
Pernod's West Face is the tallest wall in the Wine Spires, and that is the test. From the bench camp, continue up and right, east, passing A couple of minor buttresses, to gain a broad talus and scree gully that runs directly to the base of that wall.

So the count is: two minor buttresses passed, then one broad gully, then the biggest wall in the group. If the wall above you is not obviously the largest thing here, you have stopped at one of the buttresses you were supposed to pass.

The critical difference from every other route in this basin, and it is the thing that makes this approach distinct: this route does not go to Burgundy Col. It leaves the main Burgundy Col trail at the bench. If you are grinding up loose scree toward a notch between two spires, you are on the Burgundy Col trail and have missed the turn at the bench.

The last few hundred feet of the gully are loose ball-bearing scree over slab, with cairns marking the better line. Helmets should go on well before entering the gully because of rockfall from any party above.

Eight pitches at 5.10-plus R. Descent is not back down this face: rappel east down the gully to the Pernod-Chablis Notch, then a couple more rappels down steep slabs to the neve below, three rappels total, on two 60 m ropes. From the neve, trend north around the base of Chianti Spire and climb back up to Burgundy Col, then descend the climbers' path to the bench and the boot path to the highway.

So you come down the other side and walk out past a col you never visited on the way in. Budget real time: the three rappels only reach the neve, after which there is a substantial re-ascent to the col before the walk-off begins.

days.note: From the Hwy 20 pullout (~MP 166-167, just past Cutthroat Lake Rd), a climbers' trail drops to a creek crossing then climbs steeply to the flat bench camp used by west-face parties. Most parties camp here rather than push on to Burgundy Col, since the West Face is gained via a gully right from the bench, not over the col.
days.title: Approach to bench camp
days.objective: Bivy at the ~6,500 ft bench below Pernod's west face

days.note: An early start reaches the base via the approach gully at first light. The route is sustained for a Wine Spires line (grade III-IV, 5.10+) and typically takes most of a day; the descent is a multi-pitch rappel down the standard line before hiking back out past the bench and down to the highway.
days.title: Climb the Direct West Face, summit, descend to the car

schedule.label: Leave bench camp
schedule.detail: Break camp or leave it pitched and rack up.

schedule.label: Reach base of West Face
schedule.detail: Short scramble up the approach gully from the bench.

schedule.label: Top out on Pernod's summit
schedule.detail: Roughly 7-7.5 hours of climbing for a competent party.

schedule.label: Begin rappel descent
schedule.detail: Multiple rappels down the standard descent line.

schedule.label: Back at bench camp / hike out
schedule.detail: Pack up and hike down to the highway pullout.

days.objective: Send the 8-pitch 5.10+ Direct West Face and get back to the trailhead

itinerary.totalNote: A demanding 2-day outing: bivy at the ~6,500 ft bench below the west face, then a long, sustained climbing day (8 pitches, 5.10+) with a full multi-rappel descent back to the car — roughly 12-13 hours car-to-car on summit day.
